Three hypotheses for closing the referral loop

Dental Demand Labs · MENG 570 · October 25, 2026

Problem and evolution

A specialist needs to return a useful report after treating a referred patient. Our earlier discovery narrowed broad administrative work to drafting, reviewing and returning that report. One periodontist interview directly grounds the specialist task. Recipient and coordinator needs remain hypotheses to test.

Shared approach, different questions

Prototype / persona Hypothesis and test task
A · Dr. Arjun Patel, owner-periodontist Recording a consented fictional visit can reduce re-entry. A transcript and source beside an editable letter may support accurate review. Load the audio, confirm permission, prepare fields, check the source, acknowledge the missing radiograph, confirm recipient and approve.
B · Dr. Elena Ruiz, referring dentist An approved brief organized around action, owner and timing may make the handoff easier to interpret. Identify who shares the earlier radiograph and when, then verify the full approved report.
C · Maya Chen, assistant / coordinator Visible ownership and approval states may let a coordinator prepare and return a report while retaining specialist approval. Move a case from Prepare through specialist review to approved export; try a missing-note case.

Voice workflow

Permission → recording → AI transcript and quoted fields → editable letter → specialist review and recipient confirmation → approved export. Microphone capture and audio/text AI work in A. Case identifiers and destination are supplied by the tester, never inferred from speech. Edit the transcript to correct it, then prepare a new report. Changed content clears approval. Unstated information remains visible.

The sample is a synthetic fictional conversation. The prepared-example button is a clearly labelled fixed fallback; it does not call AI. Use fictional test data only. A real recording or transcript is sent to the hosted AI service when you request processing. This is a class prototype with no production privacy or clinical validation.

Working and simulated

Working: recording, audio playback, AI transcription and field extraction in A, editable drafts, review and recipient gates, approval invalidation, TXT/HTML export, B/C state transitions and observation records. Simulated: B/C sample drafting, demo role identities, practice handoff, transmission and receipts. Export does not send an email.

Product decisions

We keep voice input in A so B and C can test recipient clarity and team ownership. We retain clinician review, explicit unknowns, and the existing authorized return channel. We defer practice-management integration, autonomous sending, diagnosis and EHR replacement until need, reliability and workflow value are tested.

Testing plan

Observe task completion, missed or invented facts, help required and review time against the current workflow within each role. Use two prototype cases, including incomplete information. Class preference is a signal for the next customer test; it does not establish clinical accuracy, willingness to pay or profitability. No customer outcomes or class votes are claimed here.

Submission and rehearsal

Submit three clickable links, the presentation slides, the recorded explanation/demo, and the attributed prompt log (five actual initial build exchanges per prototype). The source log contains 18 preserved exchanges total. Current implementation notes are separate from that historical record. Do two actual team rehearsals and record timing/issues before submission.

The package does not itself prove a team rehearsal, customer test or Canvas submission. The team must complete those actions.
